chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged between the people of the city regarding the water sources of the palm trees, that the benefit of one should not be prevented, and he judged between the people of the desert that the surplus water should not be prevented in order to prevent the surplus of fodder, and he said: 'No harm and no causing harm.'

key_terms.لَا ضَرَرَ وَ لَا ضِرَارَ: no harm and no causing harm
key_terms.مَشَارِبِ النَّخْلِ: water sources of the palm trees

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on preventing water usage to protect fodder or other resources?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) citing the Prophet’s (PBUH) judicial rulings that established the foundational legal maxim 'la darara wa la dirar' (no harm and no causing harm) within agricultural water rights. It distinguishes between withholding the essential benefit of a resource, which is prohibited, and regulating surplus water to prevent harm to adjacent fodder, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on equitable resource distribution and the prevention of unilateral advantage at the expense of others.
